Equipment that fits a child

An adult gun is usually too long and too heavy for a child. The child leans back to hold it, the stock hits the cheek and shoulder, and after a few shots fear can set in. That is why gun fit matters even more for young shooters than for adults.

The key measure is the length of pull, the distance from the trigger to the middle of the butt pad. Youth models have a shorter, lighter stock, and some guns have an adjustable stock and comb. As the child grows, the stock is lengthened with spacers, so check the fit each season with the coach or a gun fitter.

A light 20 gauge is a common choice, as an over-and-under or a semi-automatic. A gas semi-automatic spreads the recoil over a longer time, so many shooters feel it as softer. Light-load cartridges also reduce recoil and make shooting more pleasant.

Protection must fit too: children's ear muffs or plugs, safety glasses with impact-resistant lenses and a peaked cap. A shooting vest must not be too big, or the gun will catch on it during the mount.

Parcours de Chasse – Sporting™

In Parcours de Chasse – Sporting™ the rules add one more point: children on the range outside the clubhouse must wear hearing protection at all times. Many families keep this habit at any ground.

Where this is in the rules: Chapter 8 · Hearing protection is compulsory

Clothes should be comfortable and right for the weather. At competitions in both disciplines sandals are banned, and shorts must be long, ending no more than 5 cm above the knee. Closed shoes with good grip are needed in training too. More: Clothing and shoes for the weather.

Tip: Do not rush into buying expensive kit. Start with a club gun for hire, then look at second-hand youth models. A gun of their own is worth buying once the child's interest is steady, with the coach's advice. General fit: Gun fit basics.

Key points

  • An adult gun is usually too long and heavy for a child.
  • Length of pull is the key to fit; check it each season.
  • A light 20 gauge and light-load cartridges.
  • Ear protection, glasses and vest in children's sizes.
  • Hire first; buy when the interest is steady.

Did you know?

The FITASC rules limit the gauge only from above, no larger than 12 gauge, so a 20-gauge gun is allowed in competition in both disciplines.

Check yourself · 3 questions

  1. What happens when a child shoots a gun that is too long?

    1. They lean back and feel more recoil
    2. Nothing changes; it is even easier
    3. The targets seem to fly more slowly
    4. The pattern becomes much denser
    Answer

    They lean back and feel more recoil

    A gun that is too long spoils the stance, makes recoil worse and can frighten the child.

  2. What is the length of pull?

    1. The length of the barrels to the muzzle
    2. From the trigger to the middle of the butt pad
    3. The weight of the gun with its chokes
    4. From the rib down to the top of the comb
    Answer

    From the trigger to the middle of the butt pad

    This is the measure most often changed to make a gun fit a child.

  3. When is it worth buying a child their own gun?

    1. Before the very first session at a ground
    2. Only a brand-new and very expensive model
    3. Once interest is steady, with a coach's advice
    4. As soon as the child can lift an adult gun
    Answer

    Once interest is steady, with a coach's advice

    Hire and second-hand models first; buy once it is clear the child will carry on.
